message.content: {"summary":"You made sensible attribute choices and gave a strong, scenario-specific modular-monolith recommendation in Q2. However, Q3 has an arithmetic slip and an incorrect end-to-end calculation, Q4's circuit breaker states are inverted, Q5 misapplies CAP, and your ADR lacks a negative consequence. Fixing these method-level errors would lift several criteria to the next level.","next_steps":["Redo Q3(b) and (c): check 0.00699 × 720, then multiply the order-path and payment-pair availabilities for the true end-to-end figure, showing all working to two decimals.","Rewrite the circuit breaker state machine so Closed passes calls normally, Open fails fast, and Half-Open success returns to Closed; add a tuning consideration such as threshold or timeout values.","Revisit CAP: during a partition you must trade consistency against availability, so pick one for payments and name a concrete technique (e.g., synchronous replication or a write quorum), and add a negative consequence to your ADR."],"criteria":{"C1":"Your performance and availability attributes are well justified from the lunch-hour scenario, and the performance scenario has all six parts with measurable response measures. To reach Excellent, make the availability measure measurable too — 'stay up most of the time' should become something like 'no more than 5 minutes of downtime per month' or a specific uptime percentage.","C2":"Excellent work. Your modular-monolith recommendation is justified by two trade-offs tied to the scenario — the five-developer team's infrastructure overhead and the insight that the root causes are the single VM and deployment process, not the monolith — and you explicitly acknowledge the downside. This meets the Excellent standard; keep applying this scenario-specific reasoning style elsewhere.","C3":"Part (a) is correct (99.30%). Part (b) has an arithmetic slip: 0.00699 × 720 is about 5.03 hours, not 3.5. Part (c) reports the payment-pair availability (99.9975%) as end-to-end; the correct end-to-end is 0.99800125 × 0.999975 ≈ 99.80%, or roughly 1.5 hours of downtime. Your method is sound, so careful checking of each part would move you up.","C4":"The Circuit Breaker is an appropriate pattern and you applied it to the outage, but the state machine is inverted: Closed should pass calls normally, Open should fail fast, and a successful Half-Open probe should close the breaker, not open it. Correct the mechanism and add a drawback or tuning consideration (e.g., threshold or reset timeout) to reach Excellent.","C5":"Both consistency/availability choices are reasonable and you named a concrete technique for menu browsing (Redis with a 60-second TTL). However, CAP is misapplied: during a partition you cannot 'give up partition tolerance' — you must trade consistency against availability. Name a concrete technique for the payment path (e.g., synchronous replication or a quorum write) to reach Excellent.","C6":"Your ADR has all three sections and is specific to CampusEats, with good use of the offline tablets, 4.2 s p95 and lunch-peak details. To reach Excellent, add at least one negative consequence — for example, delayed order notifications, the need for duplicate-order handling, or the operational burden of running the queue.","C7":"Your writing is clear and headings are used correctly. Two issues hold you at Proficient: Question 2 exceeds the 150-word limit (roughly 200 words), and source [2] is cited in Question 4 but missing from your reference list, which contains only [1]. Trim Q2 and complete the IEEE reference list to reach Excellent."}}
